subject: Packaging question: plan orchestration and proration options for PulseHealth
messages:

Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Plan question — seat vs throughput mapping and bundling

Hi Stephanie,

Quick one from our side as we prep for renewal: we're considering moving part of our workload from the Core plan to a Dedicated pool for low-latency user-facing routing, but we still want to keep the Core seat allotment for background batch jobs. Can you confirm how seats map to throughput in Dedicated (GPU slots / sustained rps)? Also we need clarity on bundling — specifically: priority support, 13-month audit log retention, and a request for a predictable overage cap.

We're evaluating a 12-month commit vs a 24-month commit; price sensitivity: if we commit to 12 months with a 20% uplift in committed throughput, what discount levers are available? Do you offer proration for mid-quarter tier changes?

Thanks — Emma
Emma Zhang
Director of AI Products, PulseHealth

[Signature]
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Oct 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Plan question — seat vs throughput mapping and bundling

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear summary, this is a great starting point. Short answers up front, then options below.

- Seats vs throughput: Dedicated pools are capacity-prescriptive. A single "medium" GPU slot (V100-equivalent) is sized to sustain ~150 tokens/sec for typical chat loads; we size pools by sustained throughput and guaranteed concurrency rather than one-to-one seats. We can provide a throughput simulation if you share typical request size and qps distribution.
- Proration: yes, we support prorated billing when you move between tiers mid-cycle; we can also apply a one-time credit for downgrades within the first 30 days of a tier change.
- Bundles: priority support and extended retention are add-ons that can be attached to either Core or Dedicated. Overage caps are configurable via the contract (soft cap + notification + hard cap).

Option A — Conservative (12m commit)
- 12-month committed throughput baseline (your current + 20% uplift)
- Add-ons: Priority Support, 13-month retention
- Suggested commercial: 10% committed-spend discount, onboarding credit applied as one-time invoice credit (see attachment 1).

Option B — Committed + Capacity Burst (12m, with burst)
- As A, plus 25% burst pool available at a lower-priority rate (metered) to handle peak days
- Suggested commercial: 12% discount on committed baseline, 6% blended on burst usage

Option C — Longer term (24m)
- 24-month commit for a lower per-unit price, includes a 30% onboarding credit toward usage during the first 90 days
- Suggested commercial: 18% committed-spend discount, deeper seat/feature credits

I've attached the current pricing grid and a sample amendment draft for the retention and support add-ons. If you'd like, we can run a short simulation with your traffic to give a recommended pool size and expected monthly spend under each option.

Next step: are you available for a 30-minute call Friday to go over numbers and tradeoffs?

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_pricing_v3.pdf (pdf, 1.1MB)]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Plan question — seat vs throughput mapping and bundling

Stephanie / Emma — adding pricing detail so the team has numbers to react to. These are illustrative; exact pricing subject to legal/finance review.

- Baseline monthly spend today (PulseHealth): $42,000 (Core + bursts)
- Option A (12m, +20% throughput): committed baseline ~$50k/mo
  - Proposed: 10% committed discount → $45k effective
  - Onboarding credit: $12k one-time credit applied in month 1
- Option B (12m with burst): committed baseline ~$50k + metered bursts (~$6k expected)
  - Proposed: 12% on baseline, 6% on bursts → blended ~$46k effective
- Option C (24m): committed baseline ~$48k/mo negotiated lower
  - Proposed: 18% committed discount + $18k onboarding credit distributed month 1-3

Margin constraints: finance has room to go up to 18% discount for a 24-month commit; for 12-month we should aim for 10–12% (unless PS/backfill revenue can offset). If legal signs onto the retention amendment without additional SLAs, we can maintain these numbers.

Suggested commercial ask for PulseHealth: 12-month commit with burst (Option B) + an initial 15% onboarding credit (split 60/40 usage/one-time) and a 10% committed discount. If they push for lower true committed price, counter with a 24-month commit at 18% discount + larger credit.

Deal ID: PH-2026-1057 (please attach to HubSpot)

—Ben
